### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via IdentityImportDeps (symbol, a top-level interface), runAdminImportUsers (symbol, a top-level function), INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via INTERNAL_ERROR (literal, a string literal in mapAuthApiError; a string literal in mapSetPasswordError; a string literal in vendorRefusal))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5736b86ede1272a2f1e992004b3cfc2fb082ae89` — the merge of head `8c878cc25361be8482174fec71166d0c909a09b0` into base `e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5736b86ede1272a2f1e992004b3cfc2fb082ae89 && git checkout 5736b86ede1272a2f1e992004b3cfc2fb082ae89
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e 8c878cc25361be8482174fec71166d0c909a09b0 && git checkout -B drift-repro e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e && git merge --no-ff 8c878cc25361be8482174fec71166d0c909a09b0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT at `Head-sha: 8c878cc25361be8482174fec71166d0c909a09b0` (2026-11-15T18:24Z).

- **Shape:**
  - No-card order from the security#1 seat.
  - 14 files, +468 / −31. Not governed (`check-governed-merges`: 0 paths). Patch on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`.
  - `Clause-②: no`. Non-breaking: status and code are unchanged at every site; only the message of an unclassified failure changes, and no docs page or first-party client reads that text.
  - `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Rule:** a route's unclassified internal failure is answered with the generic message and logged once. A vendor-classified refusal, a declared refusal and a 4xx refusal keep their own answer.
- **Seat review** (not contract tier: no protocol face, no narrowing). The diff was read at all four sites: `mapAuthApiError`, the service-account membership mapper, `mapSetPasswordError`, and the client-creation catch of `POST /sys-oauth-application/register`.
  - Each site applies the same three-way split, keeps status and code, logs once, and leaves the classified arms byte-identical.
  - The 4xx arm follows the repository's `resolveThrownHttpError` rule and has a control at each site.
  - No other catch in `auth-plugin.ts` moves.
- **Gates:**
  - CI on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed (Test Core 8/8, Build Core, Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates).
  - Locally: plugin-auth `Tests 5531 passed | 10 skipped`, and 76 of 76 derived gate families exited 0. Each site's ablation was red (2, 5, 1 and 1 cases) and restored.
  - Dogfood battery on this head: `Tests 3962 passed | 42 skipped (4004)`, no failures.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - A host that mounts `runSetInitialPassword` without a logger answers the generic message but logs nothing.
  - Hook-declared refusals at `mapAuthApiError` still answer the `INTERNAL_ERROR` code. That is pre-existing and unchanged here.
- **Landing:** through the merge queue, by the seat.
